findings.title: Shared validation and coercion paths are written once
findings.description: `as_integer` and `as_real` are the only numeric coercions. `_coerce` in `declarations.py` dispatches to them, and `ConfidenceRange`, `SignalEvent` and `bind_parameters` all go through the same helpers. `check_confidence` serves both `LabelSeries` and `SignalSequence`, and `require_optional_range` removes the repeated range check. I read `validation.py` and confirmed `require_instance`, `require_nonempty_str` and `require_iterable_of` behave as these modules assume. For example, `require_iterable_of` names the bad index as `field[index]`, which the tests match on. `value_checks.py` covers the edge cases: bool is rejected, int64 bounds are enforced, and `OverflowError` on huge ints is turned into `None`.

findings.title: Error handling follows the project exception rules
findings.description: The new code has no blanket catches. The only `except` clauses are `except OverflowError` in `as_real`, which has a justifying comment, and `except TypeError` in `require_iterable_of`, which re-raises. `InvalidParametersError` takes a single argument, so copy and pickle rebuild it, and the tests cover `copy.copy`, `copy.deepcopy` and pickle. The `TYPE_CHECKING`-only import of `ParameterIssue` avoids a runtime cycle between `errors.py` and `declarations.py`.

findings.title: `assert isinstance` used for type narrowing in production code
findings.description: `_require_series` calls `require_instance(...)` and then `assert isinstance(series, Series)` only to narrow the type for the checker. Python strips assertions under `-O`. That is harmless here because `require_instance` has already raised, but a `cast` or a `TypeGuard`-style helper would state the intent without relying on `assert`.

findings.title: Tests use unparameterized `np.ndarray` and `Any` helper types
findings.description: `_array` and `_mask` return bare `np.ndarray`. The Python rules require strict pyright over `tests` as well, and bare `np.ndarray` normally triggers `reportMissingTypeArgument` in strict mode. `test_labels.py` already uses `NDArray[np.float64]` and `NDArray[np.bool_]`, so aligning would remove the inconsistency. I did not run pyright, so this is unconfirmed.

findings.title: AST-based "no element loops" tests assert implementation, not behavior
findings.description: `test_confidence_module_has_no_element_loops` and its twin in `test_labels.py` pin a code-style property of the source (no `for`/`while`/list comprehension). They do not check observable behavior. They do enforce the slice's vectorization requirement mechanically. A load or latency test would be the more durable guard for that requirement. The AST tests are cheap and acceptable, but they will fail on harmless refactors such as a helper that adds a loop over a handful of names.

findings.title: Test coverage is thorough and tied to the contracts
findings.description: The tests parametrize the rejection cases (NaN, bool, out-of-range, wrong type, bad names). They also check that the permanent enum string values do not change, that bound mappings are read-only, that issue order is deterministic and that non-`str` keys are named by `repr`. The import-boundary tests assert that none of the new types is canonical (`CANONICAL_TYPE`) and that `display.py` stays independent of `series` and `declarations`, which mechanically backs D10 and D11.

structured_findings.summary: Shared validation and coercion paths are written once
Error handling follows the project exception rules
`assert isinstance` used for type narrowing in production code
Tests use unparameterized `np.ndarray` and `Any` helper types
AST-based "no element loops" tests assert implementation, not behavior
Test coverage is thorough and tied to the contracts
